title: 2850. Minimum Moves to Spread Stones Over Grid

examples.explanation: One possible sequence of moves to place one stone in each cell is: 1- Move one stone from cell (2,1) to cell (2,2). 2- Move one stone from cell (2,2) to cell (1,2). 3- Move one stone from cell (1,2) to cell (0,2). In total, it takes 3 moves to place one stone in each cell of the grid. It can be shown that 3 is the minimum number of moves required to place one stone in each cell.

One possible sequence of moves to place one stone in each cell is: 1- Move one stone from cell (0,1) to cell (0,2). 2- Move one stone from cell (0,1) to cell (1,1). 3- Move one stone from cell (2,2) to cell (1,2). 4- Move one stone from cell (2,2) to cell (2,1). In total, it takes 4 moves to place one stone in each cell of the grid. It can be shown that 4 is the minimum number of moves required to place one stone in each cell.
